name: Afro-Bench Holdout
purpose: The number we are allowed to believe. Afro-Bench itself has become partly in-sample: lexicon entries were written after reading its failures, so its score now measures the lexicon's coverage of that set as much as the router's understanding. This file is the control — prompts written to be answered by nobody, never consulted while tuning.
rules: NEVER add a lexicon phrase, manifest synonym or ranking rule because a case here failed. Fix the general mechanism, or leave it failing and record it.
If a case here is used to guide a change, delete it from this file and write a new one. A holdout consulted twice is not a holdout.
Prompts are deliberately harder than Afro-Bench: heavy pidgin, indirect phrasing, and domains with thin tool vocabulary.
Report the holdout number next to the Afro-Bench number, always. Quoting the tuned score alone is the exact dishonesty this file exists to prevent.

history.note: first run; routing generalises poorly, calibration generalises well
